messages.content: What's the current traffic condition in New York?

function.name: geocode_address
function.description: Transforms a description of a location (like a pair of coordinates, an address, or a name of a place) to a location on the Earth's surface. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

address.description: The address that needs to be geocoded.

locale.description: Preferred locale for the returned address information. (Optional) Default: None

message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have real‑time traffic feeds built into this chat interface. To get up‑to‑date traffic conditions for New York City you’ll want to check one of the following:

| Service | How to Use |
|---------|------------|
| **Google Maps** | Search “New York” → tap the map’s bottom panel → choose “Traffic.” You’ll see color‑coded lanes and estimated travel times. |
| **Waze** | Open the app, set your destination, and it will overlay live congestion hotspots. |
| **City & County DOT sites** | NYC Department of Transportation publishes traffic camera streams and incident reports at https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/traffic.shtml. |
| **Navigation apps** | Apple Maps, HERE, TomTom, etc., all show live traffic overlays when you search for routes. |

If you’re looking for historical patterns—e.g., typical rush hour delays—you could look at city transportation dashboards or open datasets such as NYC Taxi Trip Data or the NYPD's traffic crash database. Let me know if you'd like help pulling out specific statistics or visualizing past trends!
